findings.issue_text: [BUG] Negative-offset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (paginator.py:876) raises ValueError/AssertionError because Django querysets don't support negative indexing, causing 500 errors for crafted cursors with negative offsets; same issue in BasePaginator.get_result (~line 180) when cursor.is_prev and offset < 0

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (paginator.py:846) calls math.floor/math.ceil on raw datetime field values, raising TypeError since datetime is not a number, so the optimized_pagination=true path with datetime keys always crashes

[BUG] organization_auditlogs.py:~72 references organization_context.member.has_global_access which is not defined in scope, causing NameError and a 500 on every GET to /organizations/<org_slug>/audit-logs/

[ADVISORY] paginator.py:824 OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key silently depends on the module-level math import with no local guarantee; refactoring/pruning imports would break this class with NameError

[ADVISORY] organization_auditlogs.py:~70 gates new behavior on raw query param optimized_pagination with no feature flag or way to disable per-organization, creating a two-paginator public API where the same cursor can yield different results or 500s depending on query param and superuser status

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:870 executes queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start_offset when cursor.offset < 0 and enable_advanced_features=True, but Django querysets raise AssertionError for negative indexing; the admin-only optimized path returns a 500 and negative offset traversal cannot work

[BUG] organization_auditlogs.py:75 reads organization_context.member.has_global_access but organization_context is never defined in the method, so the optimized branch raises NameError and requests with ?optimized_pagination=true from a superuser crash with a 500

[BUG] BasePaginator.get_result (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-185) preserves offset verbatim for prev cursors (start_offset = offset when cursor.is_prev), so a prev cursor with a negative offset hits the same Django negative-slice AssertionError; the change enables negative offsets without clamping them on the prev path, breaking all existing BasePaginator consumers with malformed cursors

[ADVISORY] No tests in the diff cover the new paginator class, request parameter, or modified slicing logic; no spec asserts output parity with DateTimePaginator, the admin gate, or prev/next cursor round-trips, so a regression in shared slicing breaks every cursor-paginated endpoint with no signal

[ADVISORY] The optimized pagination behavior is gated only on a raw query param optimized_pagination with no feature flag, options entry, or kill switch; the admin gate bypasses normal org-scoped permission semantics and no test verifies the queryset filters are preserved on the optimized path

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (paginator.py:874) duplicates the float-floor/ceil key logic from DateTimePaginator instead of reusing a shared implementation, and the copy has already drifted (adds an int() wrapper the originals lack), so future key fixes must be made in two places

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (paginator.py:830-838) is a near-verbatim copy of OffsetPaginator/base get_result body; the duplicated trimming branch uses the original offset instead of start_offset, computing wrong results for the negative-offset path

[BUG] BasePaginator.get_result changes offset slicing for every paginator, not just the new optimized path; negative offsets now pass raw into queryset slicing, causing Django to index from the end and return wrong-page data on any endpoint with negative-offset cursors

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator's enable_advanced_features path is dead plumbing: nothing produces negative-offset cursors, so the optimization is functionally identical to existing OffsetPaginator and provides no performance benefit

[ADVISORY] Scope drift: authorization-gated feature (is_superuser or has_global_access) and raw optimized_pagination query-param toggle are not traceable to the performance requirement; non-admin users silently get the slow path

[ADVISORY] Rolling-deploy skew: new behavior gated on raw query param with no feature flag or API versioning, so it can't be disabled without a deploy and old/new code serve different semantics for identical URLs

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor on the datetime order key, raising TypeError and returning 500 on previous-page requests — the paginator cannot work for the endpoint it was written for

[ADVISORY] ~55 lines of copy-paste duplication of OffsetPaginator.get_result in OptimizedCursorPaginator; the implementations have already drifted, and future cursor-semantics changes must be made in three places

[ADVISORY] No test coverage for the new negative-offset slicing branch in BasePaginator.get_result or the entire OptimizedCursorPaginator class, so a regression in shared get_result offset clamping could break every paginated API endpoint with no failing test
[BUG] paginate() called with enable_advanced_features=True kwarg that Endpoint.paginate() does not accept, causing TypeError and 500 on the optimized path
[BUG] organization_context is undefined in get(), causing NameError and 500 on every GET of the endpoint
[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses int(math.floor(value)) which raises TypeError for datetime keys used by this endpoint
[BUG] Negative-offset branch feeds negative start indices to Django ORM slicing, anchoring to the end of the queryset and making pagination nondeterministic
[ADVISORY] BasePaginator.get_result slicing rewritten to branch on cursor.is_prev, silently changing behavior for forward cursors with negative offsets across all paginators
[ADVISORY] New behavior gated on raw query parameter optimized_pagination with no feature flag or documentation; same cursor token yields different pages based on caller identity
[ADVISORY] ~95 lines of new pagination logic (OptimizedCursorPaginator) with zero test coverage in the diff
[ADVISORY] Prev-cursor trimming condition len(results) == offset + limit + extra is dead code because results sliced from start_offset have max length limit + extra, causing duplicated boundary rows
[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator is a near-total duplicate of OffsetPaginator.get_result with drifted logic, a parallel-maintenance hazard

[BUG] organization_auditlogs.py:73-90 — Pagination performance PR silently swaps in a permission-gated capability change: a different paginator with different semantics (negative offsets, access beyond normal pagination bounds) enabled only for superusers/global-access members behind an undocumented `optimized_pagination` param, causing divergent pagination contracts per user on the same endpoint.

[BUG] paginator.py:179-185 — Change to shared BasePaginator.get_result slicing logic alters behavior of every existing paginator: forward cursors clamp negative offsets to 0 while prev cursors use the raw offset, silently changing results for consumers who never opted into this optimization.

[ADVISORY] paginator.py:819+ — Intent drift: stated purpose migrated from faster pagination to enabling access to data beyond normal pagination bounds via negative offsets, bypassing the pagination-boundary invariant; should be stripped back to pure performance work or explicitly re-reviewed as a new capability.

[ADVISORY] organization_auditlogs.py:74 — The `optimized_pagination` query param is the sole gate for the new code path with no feature flag, options entry, or API documentation, so operators cannot disable the new paginator without a code deploy.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (paginator.py:858): with enable_advanced_features on, a client-supplied cursor with negative offset causes queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start, raising Django's ValueError ('Negative indices are not allowed') and a 500 — a trivially triggerable DoS on the audit-log endpoint. The comment claiming Django handles negative slicing is false.

[BUG] DateTimePaginator.get_result (paginator.py:183-186): the non-optimized path now passes a raw client-controlled negative offset through unchanged when is_prev is set, producing queryset[-100:...] and the same negative-index ValueError — crash reachable on the default code path by any user with OrganizationAuditPermission via a tampered prev cursor.

[ADVISORY] Authorization for advanced features relies only on comments claiming 'permissions are checked at the queryset level'; nothing in OptimizedCursorPaginator re-verifies queryset scoping, so any future caller passing enable_advanced_features=True with a broader queryset inherits unbounded offset traversal (IDOR-shaped footgun).

[ADVISORY] New behavior gated only on the raw query parameter optimized_pagination=true with no feature flag, options entry, or env var, so operators cannot disable the optimized path without a code deploy/rollback during an incident.
New paginator class, endpoint branch, and negative-offset slicing added without any test coverage in the diff

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:850: when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, queryset[start_offset:stop] uses a negative start_offset, causing Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ to raise ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported, so every request to /api/0/organizations/<slug>/auditlogs/?optimized_pagination=true with a negative-offset cursor returns a 500

[BUG] BasePaginator.get_result at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845-848: the rewrite start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset removes the clamp for is_prev cursors, so a negative decoded offset makes queryset[offset:stop] hit the same Django negative-slice ValueError; since Cursor.__init__ (cursors.py:26) now blesses negative int(offset), any client-crafted ?cursor= with negative offset crashes the previously-working endpoint for all users

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:863: with order_by="-datetime" the key is a timezone-aware datetime, and math.floor(value) on a datetime raises TypeError, so every build_cursor call throws a 500 before any result set is returned — the optimized path is dead-on-arrival for the auditlogs endpoint

[ADVISORY] src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:25-28: the comment documents negative offsets as supported, but nothing downstream bounds or normalizes the offset, so future paginators trusting the documented contract will slice negatively and crash; the doc comment is a contract the code cannot honor and could lead engineers to re-introduce out-of-bounds data access

[BUG] Negative-offset slice `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result raises Django's AssertionError 'Negative indexing is not supported', causing a 500 for any request hitting the advanced-features branch with a negative-offset cursor; the optimization path is entirely unrunnable and the comment claiming Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically is false

[BUG] get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to a datetime value (paginator ordered by '-datetime'), raising TypeError since datetime doesn't define __round__, so any code path reaching get_item_key (prev-page boundary filter or build_cursor on every request) returns a 500 on the optimized path and prev-page requests can never be served

[BUG] With negative offset, `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` can never be true since len(results) >= 0, so the prev-page trailing-element trim silently never executes, causing prev-page responses to include a duplicate boundary row with a 200 and no error surfaced

[ADVISORY] organization_auditlogs.py dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access without a None check; for control-silo requests where member is None (superuser not a member of the org), this raises AttributeError → 500 instead of falling through to the default paginator, and it's evaluated eagerly even when use_optimized is false

[ADVISORY] The optimized_pagination=true behavior is gated on a raw query param with no feature flag or way to disable without a code deploy, and the two paginator branches produce structurally different cursors for the same dataset, causing silently different boundary/dedup behavior (duplicated or skipped rows, 200) if a client switches paths mid-traversal

[ADVISORY] The BasePaginator.get_result change clamps negative offsets to 0 on the non-prev path while the prev path keeps raw negative offsets and the new OptimizedCursorPaginator adds a third behavior, so three inconsistent offset semantics coexist in the shared base class — a cursor produced under one regime consumed under another silently returns a different page, a change-safety hazard for all existing DateTimePaginator/OffsetPaginator callers

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Negative-offset slicing in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (paginator.py:876) raises ValueError/AssertionError because Django querysets don't support negative indexing, causing 500 errors for crafted cursors with negative offsets; same issue in BasePaginator.get_result (~line 180) when cursor.is_prev and offset < 0

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (paginator.py:846) calls math.floor/math.ceil on raw datetime field values, raising TypeError since datetime is not a number, so the optimized_pagination=true path with datetime keys always crashes

[BUG] organization_auditlogs.py:~72 references organization_context.member.has_global_access which is not defined in scope, causing NameError and a 500 on every GET to /organizations/<org_slug>/audit-logs/

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py` the new code introduces `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, but the diff shows no definition or assignment for `organization_context` within the `get()` method (or imports). This would raise a `NameError` when that line executes, breaking the endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] paginator.py:824 OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key silently depends on the module-level math import with no local guarantee; refactoring/pruning imports would break this class with NameError

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calling `math.floor/ceil`, but it does not show the module imports at the top of `paginator.py`, so we cannot verify whether `math` is (or isn’t) imported at module scope. The finding’s claim about a guaranteed `NameError` is therefore not grounded in the diff, and the rest is speculative (“refactoring/pruning imports would break”), which is not a concrete defect evidenced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] organization_auditlogs.py:~70 gates new behavior on raw query param optimized_pagination with no feature flag or way to disable per-organization, creating a two-paginator public API where the same cursor can yield different results or 500s depending on query param and superuser status

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a new client-controlled switch `optimized_pagination` (`request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) that selects a different paginator class (`OptimizedCursorPaginator` vs `DateTimePaginator`) based on user/org access (`request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`). There is no feature flag, org setting, or server-side rollout control shown, so this effectively creates two pagination behaviors for the same endpoint keyed off a raw query param and privilege. That’s a concrete API/rollout/consistency concern grounded in the diff, even if specific “500s” or cursor incompatibility can’t be fully proven from the snippet alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:870 executes queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start_offset when cursor.offset < 0 and enable_advanced_features=True, but Django querysets raise AssertionError for negative indexing; the admin-only optimized path returns a 500 and negative offset traversal cannot work

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an admin-only optimized path where `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` explicitly allows `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `cursor.offset < 0` and then executes `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices/slice bounds (commonly raising an `AssertionError`), so this branch is very likely to 500 whenever a negative offset cursor is provided, contradicting the comment that the ORM “properly handles negative slicing automatically.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] organization_auditlogs.py:75 reads organization_context.member.has_global_access but organization_context is never defined in the method, so the optimized branch raises NameError and requests with ?optimized_pagination=true from a superuser crash with a 500

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `organization_auditlogs.py` sets `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`, but within the shown method body there is no definition/import of `organization_context`. If it is not a function parameter (not visible in this diff context), this reference would raise a `NameError` when the expression is evaluated (including when `optimized_pagination=true` is used and `is_superuser` is False).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BasePaginator.get_result (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-185) preserves offset verbatim for prev cursors (start_offset = offset when cursor.is_prev), so a prev cursor with a negative offset hits the same Django negative-slice AssertionError; the change enables negative offsets without clamping them on the prev path, breaking all existing BasePaginator consumers with malformed cursors

adjudication.rationale: The diff does keep `start_offset = offset` when `cursor.is_prev` in `BasePaginator.get_result`, which could allow negative slicing if a negative offset ever appears. However, the PR did not newly introduce that behavior for prev cursors: the previous code also sliced with `queryset[offset:stop]` (using `offset` verbatim) regardless of direction, so a negative offset would have behaved the same before. The claim that this change "enables negative offsets" and "breaks all existing BasePaginator consumers" is not verifiable from the diff and appears overstated; the only clear change is clamping non-prev offsets to `>= 0`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No tests in the diff cover the new paginator class, request parameter, or modified slicing logic; no spec asserts output parity with DateTimePaginator, the admin gate, or prev/next cursor round-trips, so a regression in shared slicing breaks every cursor-paginated endpoint with no signal

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial new behavior (new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, new `optimized_pagination` request flag + admin gating in `organization_auditlogs.py`, and modified shared slicing logic in `paginator.py` using `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). No test files or assertions are added in the diff to validate output parity, cursor prev/next round-trips, or the admin-only gate. While this isn’t itself a verifiable defect, it is a specific, diff-grounded risk given the shared paginator logic change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The optimized pagination behavior is gated only on a raw query param optimized_pagination with no feature flag, options entry, or kill switch; the admin gate bypasses normal org-scoped permission semantics and no test verifies the queryset filters are preserved on the optimized path

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the optimized path is enabled purely via a raw query param (`use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) plus an admin-ish gate (`request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`), with no feature flag/kill switch or API option exposure in this change. It also introduces nontrivial alternate pagination behavior (`OptimizedCursorPaginator` and `enable_advanced_features=True`) without any accompanying tests in the diff to ensure the same `queryset` filters/ordering semantics are preserved across both branches. The claim about bypassing org-scoped permissions is not directly provable from the diff (the same `queryset` is used), so the actionable part here is the lack of a controlled rollout mechanism and missing coverage for the new branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (paginator.py:874) duplicates the float-floor/ceil key logic from DateTimePaginator instead of reusing a shared implementation, and the copy has already drifted (adds an int() wrapper the originals lack), so future key fixes must be made in two places

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` uses `math.floor/ceil` and wraps the result in `int(...)`, but it does not show the existing `DateTimePaginator.get_item_key` implementation. Therefore the claim that this logic is duplicated from `DateTimePaginator` and has already drifted (specifically, that the originals lack the `int()` wrapper) cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result (paginator.py:830-838) is a near-verbatim copy of OffsetPaginator/base get_result body; the duplicated trimming branch uses the original offset instead of start_offset, computing wrong results for the negative-offset path

adjudication.rationale: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, the only trimming branch that uses `offset` (`elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra: ...`) executes only when `cursor.is_prev and cursor.value`. In that case, both code paths set `start_offset` equal to `offset` (`start_offset = cursor.offset` in the negative-offset path, and `start_offset = offset` in the non-advanced `is_prev` path), so there is no `offset` vs `start_offset` mismatch to cause wrong results specifically for the negative-offset path. The finding’s claimed defect is not verifiable from the diff (though the method is indeed largely duplicated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BasePaginator.get_result changes offset slicing for every paginator, not just the new optimized path; negative offsets now pass raw into queryset slicing, causing Django to index from the end and return wrong-page data on any endpoint with negative-offset cursors

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `BasePaginator.get_result` for all users, but it does *not* newly introduce “raw negative offset” slicing in the way described: previously it already did `queryset[offset:stop]` (so a negative `offset` would have been passed through then as well). The new code actually clamps negative offsets to 0 for the non-`is_prev` path (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). Also, the claim that Django will “index from the end” on negative queryset slicing is not supported by the diff (and Django typically rejects negative queryset slicing rather than indexing from the end).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator's enable_advanced_features path is dead plumbing: nothing produces negative-offset cursors, so the optimization is functionally identical to existing OffsetPaginator and provides no performance benefit

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `OptimizedCursorPaginator` has a special branch only when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, but the diff does not show how cursors are produced/parsed (e.g., whether `build_cursor` or request cursor parsing can yield negative offsets). Since `Cursor.offset` is simply `int(offset)` with no clamping, negative offsets could be supplied or generated elsewhere; the claim that "nothing produces negative-offset cursors" is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Scope drift: authorization-gated feature (is_superuser or has_global_access) and raw optimized_pagination query-param toggle are not traceable to the performance requirement; non-admin users silently get the slow path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `optimized_pagination=true` query param and gates the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` path behind `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` in `organization_auditlogs.py`. Non-admins silently fall back to `DateTimePaginator`. This is a real, diff-grounded scope/architecture concern (feature toggle + authorization gating embedded in endpoint logic) but not a verifiable correctness/security defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Rolling-deploy skew: new behavior gated on raw query param with no feature flag or API versioning, so it can't be disabled without a deploy and old/new code serve different semantics for identical URLs

adjudication.rationale: The endpoint now conditionally switches pagination behavior based on a raw query parameter (`use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"`) and runtime auth (`enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`) to choose `OptimizedCursorPaginator` vs `DateTimePaginator`. This introduces a rolling-deploy skew risk: during a deploy, identical URLs with `?optimized_pagination=true` can yield different pagination semantics/cursor behavior depending on which app version serves the request, and there’s no feature flag/API versioning shown in the diff to coordinate/disable it without another deploy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor on the datetime order key, raising TypeError and returning 500 on previous-page requests — the paginator cannot work for the endpoint it was written for

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the optimized path paginates with `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` and `order_by="-datetime"`. `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key()` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then applies `math.floor/ceil` and `int(...)`. For this endpoint, `self.key` is expected to correspond to the `datetime` ordering field, so `value` will be a `datetime` object. `math.floor()`/`math.ceil()` on a `datetime` raises `TypeError`, causing a 500 when cursor keys are computed (e.g., prev/next cursor building).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ~55 lines of copy-paste duplication of OffsetPaginator.get_result in OptimizedCursorPaginator; the implementations have already drifted, and future cursor-semantics changes must be made in three places

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result(...)`, which largely duplicates the existing paginator `get_result` logic (cursor normalization, queryset build, hits counting, offset/extra handling, prev trimming/reverse, `build_cursor`, post_query_filter). This is clear copy-paste duplication within `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`, and the new implementation already diverges via the `enable_advanced_features` negative-offset branch and slightly different slicing/offset handling. That creates a real maintenance/architecture risk: future cursor/offset semantics changes in the existing paginator(s) would need to be replicated here as well.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test coverage for the new negative-offset slicing branch in BasePaginator.get_result or the entire OptimizedCursorPaginator class, so a regression in shared get_result offset clamping could break every paginated API endpoint with no failing test

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new, nontrivial pagination behavior paths—(1) a new offset-clamping/prev-branch change in `BasePaginator.get_result` (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`) and (2) an entirely new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with an `enable_advanced_features` path that explicitly allows negative slicing (`queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset = cursor.offset` if negative). The diff contains no accompanying tests for these branches/classes, so a regression in this shared pagination logic could impact many paginated endpoints without being caught by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] paginate() called with enable_advanced_features=True kwarg that Endpoint.paginate() does not accept, causing TypeError and 500 on the optimized path

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `self.paginate(..., enable_advanced_features=True)` being passed in the optimized branch, but it does not include the definition/signature of `Endpoint.paginate()` (or `self.paginate`) to verify whether it rejects unknown kwargs. Since the claim of a guaranteed `TypeError` depends on code not shown in the diff, the finding is not verifiable from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] organization_context is undefined in get(), causing NameError and 500 on every GET of the endpoint

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Negative-offset branch feeds negative start indices to Django ORM slicing, anchoring to the end of the queryset and making pagination nondeterministic

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Negative-offset slice `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result raises Django's AssertionError 'Negative indexing is not supported', causing a 500 for any request hitting the advanced-features branch with a negative-offset cursor; the optimization path is entirely unrunnable and the comment claiming Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically is false

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to a datetime value (paginator ordered by '-datetime'), raising TypeError since datetime doesn't define __round__, so any code path reaching get_item_key (prev-page boundary filter or build_cursor on every request) returns a 500 on the optimized path and prev-page requests can never be served

If `self.key` corresponds to the ordering field (here `datetime`), `value` will be a `datetime` object, and `math.floor/ceil(datetime)` raises `TypeError` (expects a real number). Since `build_cursor(...)` is invoked every `get_result()` call and uses `key=self.get_item_key`, this would cause 500s whenever the optimized paginator is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] With negative offset, `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` can never be true since len(results) >= 0, so the prev-page trailing-element trim silently never executes, causing prev-page responses to include a duplicate boundary row with a 200 and no error surfaced

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The optimized_pagination=true behavior is gated on a raw query param with no feature flag or way to disable without a code deploy, and the two paginator branches produce structurally different cursors for the same dataset, causing silently different boundary/dedup behavior (duplicated or skipped rows, 200) if a client switches paths mid-traversal

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The BasePaginator.get_result change clamps negative offsets to 0 on the non-prev path while the prev path keeps raw negative offsets and the new OptimizedCursorPaginator adds a third behavior, so three inconsistent offset semantics coexist in the shared base class — a cursor produced under one regime consumed under another silently returns a different page, a change-safety hazard for all existing DateTimePaginator/OffsetPaginator callers

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce multiple offset-handling regimes. In `BasePaginator.get_result`, the new logic clamps `offset` to `>=0` only when `not cursor.is_prev` (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`), while the `is_prev` path continues to use the raw `offset` (which could be negative). Separately, the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` adds a third behavior: when `enable_advanced_features` and `cursor.offset < 0`, it explicitly allows a negative `start_offset` (`start_offset = cursor.offset`) and slices the queryset with it; otherwise it uses the same clamp-vs-prev behavior. This does create inconsistent semantics for the same serialized cursor fields (`cursor.offset`, `cursor.is_prev`) depending on which paginator consumes them, which is a change-safety/compatibility concern grounded in the shown code. However, the diff alone does not prove that cursors are actually reused across paginator classes in production, so the finding is more of an architectural/behavioral hazard than a directly verifiable broken behavior.
